dossier.purpose: Agent Console (LockedIn Labs, MIT, v0.4.1) is a zero-dependency Node.js (>=22) local web console with an optional multi-machine hub. It reads the JSONL transcripts that Claude Code and Codex already write on disk and turns them into per-response token events in four disjoint classes (uncached input, output, cache write with a 5m/1h split when Claude Code reports it, cache read). It de-duplicates streamed lines, forked-subagent copies and copied transcripts, and adds context/cache-health signals, live alerts and offline list-price cost estimates. Fact for the need's question (which single tool measures provider usage from the local Claude Code and Codex logs): this one program does that for both tools from local transcripts (lib/collector/parsers.js:133-170, 262-269; docs/accounting.md:108-127), not from provider APIs or invoices (docs/accounting.md:388-390). It is read-only observability: a repo-wide search found no feature that supplies task context to agents, keeps recoverable originals of artifacts, or measures artifact/context reductions ('compaction' appears only as an accounting rule, docs/accounting.md:142,145), and it ships no MCP server (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:354-360). Facts were read from the v0.4.1 checkout with read/search tools only; no code or tests were executed.

claims.claim: Local and team observability for Claude Code and Codex: every session's tokens, cache reads and writes, models and list-price cost, on this computer and on every connected computer, in one local console.

No account to create, no package install and no build step: `node bin/agent-console.mjs --open` reads the Claude Code and Codex history already on the computer and opens the console, signed in, normally at http://127.0.0.1:6787.

Nothing leaves a machine but counts (model ids, minute timestamps, token counts, salted hashes), never a prompt, reply, file path or file contents; a test pushes planted canaries through the real reporter and hub and checks every byte on the wire. The console itself sends no telemetry, no update check, no account; three opt-ins (--share-project-names, --share-alerts, --share-tool-activity) are off unless passed.

Tokens are split into cache read, cache write (by cache lifetime), output and uncached input; totals, estimate, message count and per-class shares follow one period (1 h, 24 h, 7 d, 30 d); usage lines that could not be counted are counted by reason and shown beside the figures, never silently dropped.
Unknown is not zero: a record that did not report a token class makes the total a floor, and a model with no verified list price is left out of the dollar figure rather than priced at $0.
Copied transcripts count once: record ids come from the transcript itself, not from file location, so the same session read on two machines is one set of events.
Dollars are estimates at standard API list prices from a dated, offline table (lib/collector/prices.json); not an invoice or subscription charge; tokens measure usage, not productivity.

Context and cache health: a session is flagged when an input reading reaches 160,000 tokens, or reaches 80,000 and doubles from the first retained reading; the last 16 readings are shown and the hub keeps at most 128 per session; idle-gap and possible-prefix-rewrite signals carry an estimated extra cost; the logs do not prove the cause.

Optional --interop enables a local Prometheus /metrics endpoint and local ingest of Claude Code OpenTelemetry and Kong/LiteLLM token metrics, shown in a Telemetry panel kept separate from transcript totals so one request is never added twice; read and ingest use separate credentials.
A dependency-free shared analysis core is exported as @lockedinlabs/agent-console/analysis (ANALYSIS_VERSION 1, contextHealth and others); the package is not on the npm registry.
The hub keeps 8 days of usage by default (--retention-days) in ~/.agent-console/hub/; 30-day views come from daily totals kept for 400 days.

Works on macOS, Linux and Windows (console, joining/reporting, Projects view with git); CI runs the whole suite including the multi-process privacy test and the package smoke test on all three with Node 22 and 24.

Distribution status as stated: the GitHub v0.4.1 release has a Node.js package and standalone files for macOS, Linux and Windows; @lockedinlabs/agent-console is not published to npm; the Homebrew tap and a container image are not verified as available.

Claude Code or Codex can install it from the repository URL by following INSTALL.md; an optional `policy` command compiles agent-policy.yaml into Claude Code project agents, settings and hooks (nothing is installed by starting the dashboard; hard token/dollar budget enforcement is not available from the native launch hook).

install.method: Run from source with git and Node.js 22+ (Linux, macOS, Windows; no build step)
install.command:
git clone https://github.com/LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.git
cd agent-console
node bin/agent-console.mjs --open

install.method: npm global install of the v0.4.1 GitHub release archive (the registry package is not published)
npx of the v0.4.1 GitHub release archive
Standalone executable (Node.js inside) via install.sh into ~/.local/bin (Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64/x64; Linux needs glibc 2.28+)
Docker team-hub image (Linux amd64/arm64; hub only, --no-local; README says a v0.4.1 image has not been verified)
install.command:
docker volume create agent-console-state
docker run --name agent-console-hub --network host \
  -v agent-console-state:<private> \
  ghcr.io/lockedinlabs-ai/agent-console:v0.4.1

install.method: Homebrew tap (documented in the formula README, but stated as not published or verified)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - README.md:257-266 lists Linux as working and says CI runs the whole suite on Linux (ubuntu-latest, .github/workflows/ci.yml:13); the release carries agent-console-linux-x64 (docs/executables.md:13), built and smoke-tested on ubuntu-24.04 (.github/workflows/binaries.yml:66) and installed with install.sh on that runner at release (.github/workflows/release.yml:275, 287-295); the standalone build needs glibc 2.28+ (install.sh:48-65).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - WSL is not in the README support table (README.md:257-266) and no CI job runs under WSL (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13). The code is WSL-aware: it detects WSL (lib/hub/routes.js:129-132) and prints that the WSL address is usually reachable from this computer only, advising --advertise plus a port forward or mirrored networking (server.js:396-399; README.md:661). Transcripts inside WSL would be read as on Linux, but that is not stated or tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - README.md:257-266; the release carries agent-console-darwin-arm64 (docs/executables.md:11), built on macos-15 (.github/workflows/binaries.yml:64) and installed on that runner at release (.github/workflows/release.yml:273, 287-295); signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized from v0.4.1 (docs/executables.md:50-55); CI also runs macos-latest (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13).
platforms.gpu: no - not applicable: a log-reading Node.js dashboard with no GPU, CUDA or Metal code (a search of README, INSTALL, docs, lib, server.js, package.json and Dockerfile found only a roadmap note about a future NVIDIA Dynamo Prometheus adapter, docs/policy.md:168-174).

integrations.cli: yes. Binary `agent-console` (package.json:29-31). No command or only options starts the console (--open, --demo, --json prints launch details as JSON, --listen, --retention-days, --claude-root/--codex-root, --poll-ms, ...); join|report|stop|leave run the reporter; `policy diff|apply|remove|status`; `metrics-token --scope read|ingest`; --version/help (bin/agent-console.mjs:23-56; lib/config.js:180-239; lib/reporter.js:63-105; docs/policy.md:73-96). Headless inspection without the web console: `node lib/collector/collector.js --summary` prints today's (local calendar day) per-class totals as JSON and, for a machine that never enrolled, creates no state and sends nothing (lib/collector/README.md:18-22; lib/collector/collector.js:615-668, 685, 869-895). Not run in this review.
integrations.mcp: none found. The docs state the package has no MCP server, registry, proxy or gateway and that response redaction does not cover MCP traffic (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:354-360). No .mcp.json, plugin, skill or slash-command files exist in the tree (searches for SKILL.md, plugin.json, .mcp.json, .claude* and 'plugin' in README/docs found none). MCP tool calls are only counted as kind 'mcp' in the opt-in tool-activity counts (docs/COLLECTOR-CONTRACT.md:156-163).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Library: `@lockedinlabs/agent-console/analysis` (pure, dependency-free: contextHealth, alert reducer, agentTree, costPerOutcome, policy parsing, interop summaries; package.json:24-28; lib/analysis/index.js:1-8; docs/ANALYSIS.md) and `@lockedinlabs/agent-console/conformance` (synthetic Claude Code/Codex logs plus expected totals; test/conformance/index.js:1-32); the package is not on the npm registry (README.md:349-352). HTTP, loopback 127.0.0.1 only, needs the sign-in cookie and an `X-Agent-Console: 1` header: GET /api/console (per period `tokens` {total, fresh, output, cacheWrite, cacheRead, cacheWrite5m, cacheWrite1h, cacheWriteUnknownTtl}, per-class `unknown` counts, cost, lanes, context; lib/hub/aggregate.js:312-343; lib/hub/routes.js:576-642) and GET /api/projects?period=; schemas docs/console-v0.4.schema.json and docs/projects-v0.4.schema.json (the console schema documents the v0.4 additions, docs/console-v0.4.schema.json:5). Programmatic reads need the sign-in flow shown in test/hub-e2e.test.js:68-86 (start with --json, follow the printed sign-in link). With --interop and a bearer token from `metrics-token`: GET /metrics (Prometheus gauge agent_console_transcript_tokens_last_24h{kind=input|output|cache_read|cache_write}; lib/analysis/interop.js:42-48), POST /v1/metrics (OTLP/HTTP JSON) and POST /ingest/gateway/kong|litellm (lib/hub/routes.js:516-556). Reporters use POST /api/ingest over pinned TLS with a device token (docs/COLLECTOR-CONTRACT.md:297-304). The exact per-window accounting report (lib/hub/accounting.js) is imported only by tests, not by server code, the CLI or package exports.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Reads both tools' local transcripts read-only: Claude Code from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects, ~/.claude/projects and ~/.config/claude/projects; Codex from $CODEX_HOME/sessions plus archived_sessions, or ~/.codex/sessions plus ~/.codex/archived_sessions (lib/collector/collector.js:65-93; docs/accounting.md:17-35). No other tool is parsed (lib/collector/parsers.js:425-428). README and INSTALL.md are written so Claude Code or Codex can install it from the repo URL (README.md:37-40; INSTALL.md:1-6, 111-115). Claude Code only: `agent-console policy apply` writes repo-scoped .claude/agents, .claude/settings.json and a local hook (PreToolUse, PreModelSwitch) with private backups and `policy remove` (docs/policy.md:83-134; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:121-168); there is no Codex enforcement adapter (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:25-26). Claude Code's own OpenTelemetry metrics can be pointed at /v1/metrics when --interop is on (docs/INTEROP.md:47-83). No plugin, skill, slash command or mechanism for supplying context to either agent was found.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, update check, crash reporting, analytics, licence check or account, per docs (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:42-51; README.md:66-73; docs/PRINCIPLES.md:42-47; CONTRIBUTING.md:77-78) and per code. The shipped code's outbound call sites are: loopback fetches to find or sign in to an already-running console (lib/hub/port.js:33-44; lib/hub/admin.js:271-293; server.js:147); certificate-pinned HTTPS to the hub named in a join link (lib/collector/pinned.js:38-113; lib/reporter.js:342,575,797); a loopback-only probe (lib/reporter.js:305-326); and lib/collector/transport.js:314-323, which posts only to the hub or the URL the operator gives (plain HTTP only to private hosts unless allowHttp, transport.js:59-80). The UI's CSP limits connect-src to 'self' (lib/hub/http.js:27-30) and the service worker handles same-origin requests only (public/sw.js:19-34). No model API is called (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:53-57). Accounts: none; no model API key or cloud account needed (INSTALL.md:3-6). The network is used only on request: --listen opens the reporting port (default 127.0.0.1:6788) to private-range callers (public ranges need --allow-public, 100.64.0.0/10 needs --allow-cgnat; lib/hub/routes.js:189-196); join, report and leave are TLS-only (lib/hub/routes.js:212-218); the join page is plain HTTP (SECURITY.md:172-197). Downloads from github.com over HTTPS happen only when a person runs install.sh/install.ps1 or a printed join command (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:38-39; lib/invocation.js:54); whether npx contacts the npm registry depends on npm, not this code (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:59-65). What leaves a reporting machine: allowlisted usage metadata and salted hashes, plus opt-in project folder names, alert kinds and tool-call counts (README.md:555-583; lib/collector/collector.js:305-337). Local state lives under ~/.agent-console (modes 600/700, no at-rest encryption, docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md:203-205); the hub's own machine also keeps project folder names, full paths and branches in names.json for its own screen (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:97-101,114). The website sources contain no analytics (docs/website.md:3-6; no analytics or fetch calls found under site/). Repo CI, not the product, publishes OpenSSF Scorecard results to the public Scorecard API (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml:3-8,35).

languages: JavaScript (Node.js >=22; ESM .js/.mjs, plus CommonJS .cjs for the executable launcher)
HTML/CSS/vanilla JavaScript (browser UI in public/, static site in site/)

entry_points.what: The `agent-console` binary (package.json bin): checks Node >=22, then dispatches version, join|report|leave|stop (lib/reporter.js), metrics-token, policy, or no command/options (server.js); unknown words are refused (bin/agent-console.mjs:14-56).
Console + hub server main: loopback console listener, reporting listener (plain-HTTP join page and TLS ingestion), local collection, --demo (server.js:1-16, 314-350).
Reporter for another machine: join, report, stop, leave (lib/reporter.js:1-33, 63-105).
`policy diff|apply|remove|status` for Claude Code project files, with the hook it installs in lib/policy/hook.mjs and classify.mjs (bin/agent-console.mjs:35-41; docs/policy.md:83-134).
First script of the standalone executables: unpacks the embedded package into the user cache, verifies every file's SHA-256, then starts it (packaging/sea/main.cjs:1-15).

code.architecture: Local-first pipeline, Node.js standard library only. (1) Collector, lib/collector/: scanner.js picks transcript files; collector.js keeps a per-file byte cursor and a write-ahead spool and lets only the projectRecord allowlist out (collector.js:305-337); parsers.js turns one JSONL line into usage records (Claude Code: per-message running maximum shared across files so streamed lines and forked-subagent copies count once; Codex: cumulative counters to per-event deltas, per-response token_usage_record lines, fork-boundary and counter-reset rules) and counts lines it cannot count as coverage debt by reason; pricing.js + prices.json give offline list-price estimates; transport.js and pinned.js deliver batches over certificate-pinned HTTPS. (2) Hub, server.js and lib/hub/: two listeners, the console on 127.0.0.1 (cookie sign-in in admin.js; routes.js; http.js with CSP and secret redaction) and a reporting port that serves the join page over plain HTTP and ingestion over TLS by sniffing the first byte (server.js:314-334; self-signed ECDSA certificate in tls.js); registry.js (devices, single-use invitations, token verifiers), store.js (records-<day>.ndjson, minute buckets for the retention window, 400-day daily rollup, up to 128 context samples per session), aggregate.js (the /api/console payload), local.js (the hub reads its own machine in-process every --poll-ms, default 2 s), alerts.js, fleet.js, projects.js, state-lock.js. (3) lib/reporter.js (+ reporter-outbox.js, reporter-search.js) runs on other machines: join, report, stop, leave. (4) lib/analysis/: pure count-based functions (contextHealth, alerts, agentTree, costPerOutcome, policy parsing, interop summaries); lib/interop/ingest.js: opt-in OTLP/Kong/LiteLLM adapters; lib/policy/: Claude Code policy compiler and hook; lib/gitstats.js: local git evidence. (5) public/: vanilla-JS UI (console.js, join.js, network-only service worker sw.js); site/: static download page. (6) Build and release: packaging/sea (Node single-executable via postject), Dockerfile (hub image), packaging/homebrew-tap (formula template), .github/workflows, scripts/, bench/.
code.packaging_and_release: Per release (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:296-352; scripts/release-assets-check.mjs:16-23): the npm tarball lockedinlabs-agent-console-<version>.tgz (npm pack), five standalone Node-embedded executables (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64.exe) plus four .tar.gz archives (ten assets), six CycloneDX 1.5 SBOMs (*.cdx.json; .github/scripts/release-sbom.mjs:117,193-194) and SHA256SUMS (.github/workflows/release.yml:122-139); a GHCR hub image for linux/amd64 and arm64 with provenance, SBOM and an attestation (.github/workflows/ghcr.yml:95-124). Attestations: actions/attest-build-provenance over dist/* and the SBOMs, plus a per-file SBOM attestation (release.yml:140-177); verify with `gh attestation verify` (SECURITY.md:55-81); SLSA Build Level 2 self-assessed, not Level 3 (docs/security/SSDF.md:53-63). macOS executables are Developer-ID signed and notarized from v0.4.1 and the release fails without the five Apple secrets (release.yml:44-67; scripts/release-assets-check.mjs:42-44); the Windows executable is not code-signed (docs/executables.md:75-84). v0.1.0-v0.3.0 were attested under SamSnead85/agent-console (README.md:757-761). Pipeline: triggered by `release: published` (release.yml:11-13); the authorize job requires the tag to be a main commit whose main-push ci.yml, public-safety and perf runs succeeded (release.yml:18-39; scripts/release-source-check.mjs:7-32); native builds (binaries.yml), npm test, smoke:pack and upload without --clobber (release.yml:115-193); then published-install acceptance on Linux, macOS and Windows (release.yml:221-321); the npm job needs NPM_TOKEN and README states the registry package is not published (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:35-65; README.md:89). Actions are pinned to commit SHAs; Dependabot updates actions, npm and docker weekly (.github/dependabot.yml). Not verified here: that the v0.4.1 release assets exist (no network access in this review).
code.tests_and_ci: Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`, concurrency 4 by default) enumerated by scripts/test.mjs:11-35; 69 test files in test/*.test.js, every one importing node:test; plus test/conformance/ (23 synthetic Claude Code/Codex transcript files, manifest.json, expected.json, collector-records.json), test/fixtures/ and test/helpers/. Notable: test/hub-e2e.test.js (real hub and reporter processes plus a recording TLS relay as the privacy canary), test/conformance.test.js (collector to hub store to accounting to console, compared to expected totals), test/security.test.js, test/collector-parsers.test.js. `npm run lint` is `node --check` on all JS plus JSON validity, not a linter or type check (scripts/lint.mjs:1-8); `npm run smoke:pack` packs, installs into a scratch prefix and starts demo mode (scripts/pack-smoke.mjs:1-9). CI has 13 workflow files in .github/workflows/: ci.yml (3 OS x Node 22/24: npm test, smoke:pack, git diff check; lint and an npm audit of the packaging/sea lockfile on Linux/Node 24; ci.yml:9-32), perf.yml (counted-operation budgets via bench/check.mjs), public-safety.yml (gitleaks + public-content check), pr-checks.yml (changelog and screenshot rules), ui-probes.yml (Playwright + axe in a real browser, installed ad hoc in CI), binaries.yml (builds and starts every native target on its own runner), ghcr.yml (image build/start for amd64 and arm64), installers.yml and readme-install.yml (weekly and on change: run install.sh/install.ps1 and the README install line against the latest release), pages.yml (download page), scorecard.yml (OpenSSF Scorecard), release.yml and npm-publish.yml (release). CodeQL is cited in docs as running on every change (docs/security/SSDF.md:41; docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md:140-143) but there is no CodeQL workflow file in the tree, so it is configured outside it and not verifiable here. Required-check branch protection is repository configuration and not visible in the checkout (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:328-331). Tests were not executed in this review.
code.dependencies: package.json (root): 0 dependencies, 0 devDependencies (package.json:58-60); runtime is Node >=22 standard library only (server.js:18-24; lib/collector/collector.js:15-25 import only node: and relative modules; a search of lib/, server.js and bin/ for other import specifiers found only strings inside code). packaging/sea/package.json: 0 dependencies, 1 devDependency (postject 1.0.0-alpha.6, build-time only, packaging/sea/package.json:6-8) with a committed lockfile (packaging/sea/package-lock.json, transitive commander 9.5.0) installed with --ignore-scripts (.github/workflows/binaries.yml:88-89). No other manifests (a search for package.json, lockfiles, requirements, go.mod, Cargo.toml etc. found only these three). The Dockerfile base is node:22-bookworm-slim pinned by digest (Dockerfile:1). Playwright and axe-core are installed ad hoc in the UI-probes CI job only (.github/workflows/ui-probes.yml:24-30). The standalone executables embed Node.js 24 (docs/executables.md:3-8; binaries.yml:84-87).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md at the repo root: private reporting through GitHub Security Advisories; targets (not commitments) of acknowledgement in 2 business days, reproduce/CVSS in 5, fixed release for critical/high in 30 days and others in 90; only 0.4.x receives security fixes; scope and download-verification steps listed (SECURITY.md:3-81). Supporting documents: docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md, THREAT-MODEL.md, SSDF.md (maintainer self-assessment, not an audit, SSDF.md:11) and ENTERPRISE-FAQ.md.

claim_checks.claim: Measures provider usage (input, output, cache-creation and cache-read tokens) from the local logs Claude Code and Codex write.
claim_checks.evidence: Claude Code: yes - assistant message.usage input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens, plus the 5m/1h split, are read (lib/collector/parsers.js:159-170). Codex: input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens and cache_write_input_tokens are read from token_count totals or per-response token_usage_record lines (parsers.js:262-269, 271-411); uncached input is derived as input minus cached minus cache_write and is null (unknown) when cache_write_input_tokens is absent (parsers.js:357-359, 403-404), so the Codex cache-creation class depends on a field the repo can only show in synthetic fixtures (test/collector-parsers.test.js:18-19); whether real Codex logs always carry it cannot be checked from this checkout. Only these two tools are parsed (parsers.js:425-428). Classes are disjoint and total = input + output + cache read + cache write (docs/accounting.md:108-127). The source is local transcripts, not provider APIs (docs/accounting.md:388-390). Code path read, not executed.

claim_checks.claim: Nothing leaves a machine but counts; a canary test checks every byte on the wire.
claim_checks.evidence: One allowlist, projectRecord, builds every record (lib/collector/collector.js:305-337). test/hub-e2e.test.js starts real hub and reporter processes over canary-laden transcripts through a recording TLS relay that holds the hub's certificate (test/hub-e2e.test.js:1-11, 94-123, 125-145); README.md:578-583 adds the hub's files, the reporter's files and the console payload. The README's headline sentence lists only model ids, minutes, counts and hashes; records also carry the tool, subagent flag, price tier, cache TTL kind, device id, an execution-origin hash and the machine label, which README.md:555-569 and docs/COLLECTOR-CONTRACT.md:50-67 disclose.

claim_checks.claim: The console itself sends no telemetry, no update check and no account.
claim_checks.evidence: Outbound call sites in the shipped code: loopback fetches (lib/hub/port.js:33-44; lib/hub/admin.js:271-293; server.js:147), certificate-pinned HTTPS to the hub in a join link (lib/collector/pinned.js:38-113; lib/reporter.js:342,575,797), a loopback-only probe (lib/reporter.js:305-326), and lib/collector/transport.js:314-323 which posts only to the hub or operator-given URL (plain HTTP only to private hosts unless allowHttp, transport.js:59-80). CSP connect-src 'self' (lib/hub/http.js:27-30); the service worker is same-origin only (public/sw.js:19-34). Matches docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:21-51. Greps for fetch, http.request, tls.connect, net.connect, WebSocket and sendBeacon in lib/, server.js and public/ found nothing else. What npx/npm contact is outside this code (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:59-65).

claim_checks.claim: No account, no package install, no build step and no dependencies; Node.js 22 or newer.
claim_checks.evidence: package.json:58-60 (empty dependencies and devDependencies), package.json:32-34 (engines >=22), bin/agent-console.mjs:14-21 (refuses Node <22), server.js:18-24 and lib/collector/collector.js:15-25 (only node: and relative imports); a search of lib/, server.js and bin/ for other import specifiers found only strings inside code. The only dev dependency is the build-time postject (packaging/sea/package.json:6-8).

claim_checks.claim: Context and cache health: flagged at 160,000 input tokens, or 80,000 and doubling; last 16 readings; at most 128 per session; idle-gap and possible-prefix-rewrite signals with an estimated extra cost.
claim_checks.evidence: lib/analysis/context.js:32-59 (bloated = latest >= 160_000 or latest >= 80_000 with growth >= 2; samples.slice(-16); break kinds idle-gap, lifetime-unknown, possible-prefix-rewrite; extra cost = write cost minus a hypothetical cache read at table rates, lines 15-25); lib/hub/store.js:311-324 (continuation rows excluded, samples.length > 128 drops the oldest); lib/hub/aggregate.js:730 calls contextHealth per lane.

claim_checks.claim: Dollar figures are offline list-price estimates and unknown is never priced at zero.
claim_checks.evidence: lib/collector/pricing.js:71-114 returns status 'unpriced' with usd null for an unlisted model, unverified rate, unknown tier or any unreported token class. lib/collector/prices.json:1-13 (USD, basis standard-global-api-equivalent, inventoryCheckedOn 2026-09-20) holds 22 model rows (19 verified, 3 unpriced: codex-auto-review, gpt-5.3-codex-spark, gpt-reserve) and 1 alias (prices.json:435-443). Models released later are unpriced until the table is updated.

claim_checks.claim: Copied transcripts count once and totals reconcile to the token.
claim_checks.evidence: Record ids are HMACs of tool, session id and message id under the shared salt, not paths (lib/collector/collector.js:165; docs/COLLECTOR-CONTRACT.md:52); Claude messages use a per-message running maximum shared across files so forked copies add only growth (lib/collector/parsers.js:172-224, 244-254); test/conformance.test.js:1-7, 44-53 replays synthetic logs through collector, store, accounting and console and compares to expected.json to the token and 1e-9 USD (docs/accounting.md:349-353). But the expected totals are summed from project-authored synthetic ground truth (docs/accounting.md:346-347), transcripts are not reconciled with the provider's usage API or invoice (docs/accounting.md:388-390), and drops are counted per machine for a transcript copied to two machines (docs/accounting.md:393-394).

claim_checks.claim: Defaults: 8 days of minute data (1-90 configurable), 30-day views from a 400-day daily rollup, transcripts polled every 2 seconds.
claim_checks.evidence: lib/config.js:19-20, 130-132 (default 8, clamp 1-90; poll default 2000 ms); lib/hub/store.js:72 (ROLLUP_DAYS = 400); lib/hub/local.js:143 and lib/collector/collector.js:463-470 (files older than the retention window are not read); docs/MEASUREMENTS.md:7-9; docs/accounting.md:241-255 (30-day periods are marked partial where daily totals are missing). Where docs and code differ the code was preferred: lib/collector/README.md:12 says the local collector runs every five seconds, but server.js:268 passes config.pollMs (default 2000), matching README.md:671.

risks: Scope: read-only observability of provider usage. The tool 'observes; it does not route or authorize model or tool calls' (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:8-12, 21-26). A repo-wide search found no feature that supplies task context to agents, stores recoverable originals of artifacts, or measures artifact/context reductions; 'compaction' appears only as an accounting rule (docs/accounting.md:142,145), and the only separation it keeps is between transcript totals and optional OTel/gateway readings (docs/INTEROP.md:82-83, 102-105). The only originals it preserves are the project .claude files that `policy apply` overwrites (private backup, `policy remove`; docs/policy.md:90-96). No MCP server (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:354-360). The exact per-window accounting report (lib/hub/accounting.js) is imported only by tests; supported programmatic reads are the signed-in /api/console, /metrics (24 h gauges, --interop only) and `collector.js --summary` (local-day totals).

Measurement basis: counts come from transcripts the tools wrote and are not reconciled with the provider's usage API or invoice; requests a tool never logged are invisible (docs/accounting.md:388-390). Parsing depends on unofficial log formats and observed behaviour such as copied-history ids staying stable (docs/accounting.md:381-384); the conformance suite and fixtures are project-authored synthetic logs (test/conformance.test.js:1-7). Codex uncached input and cache write need cache_write_input_tokens; if absent they are unknown and totals become floors (lib/collector/parsers.js:357-359). Cost uses a static table of 22 model rows dated 2026-09-20 (lib/collector/prices.json:5; lib/collector/pricing.js:71-114). Default retention is 8 days of minute data, at most 90 (lib/config.js:19, 130-132).

Maintenance and maturity: one maintainer owns every path (.github/CODEOWNERS:1-5; docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md:188-193); main requires no reviews or signed commits and administrators can bypass required checks (THREAT-MODEL.md:188-193; docs/security/SSDF.md:21, 28). Pre-1.0 with seven versions dated 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-27 (CHANGELOG.md:3, 66, 119, 449, 537, 597, 655), a security advisory fixed in 0.2.2 (CHANGELOG.md:449-474), and upgrade rules (stop old hubs, upgrade the console before reporters; README.md:725-731; CHANGELOG.md:115-117). The repository moved from SamSnead85/agent-console and v0.1.0-v0.3.0 attestations keep the old identity (README.md:757-761). Security fixes cover 0.4.x only (SECURITY.md:32-37). The SSDF document is the maintainer's own assessment, not an audit (docs/security/SSDF.md:11).

Distribution and documentation drift: README says the npm package is not published and the Homebrew tap and container image are unverified (README.md:85-91), and it both states that v0.4.1 packages are published (README.md:88) and still says 'Until v0.4.1 packages are published' (README.md:224-229, 504-506). lib/collector/README.md:12 says the local collector runs every five seconds but the default is 2 s (lib/config.js:20; server.js:268). THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:49 names lib/prices.js, which does not exist in the tree.

Install and supply chain: the Linux/macOS installer is fetched with curl from the mutable main branch (docs/standalone-install.md:19-31). install.sh checks only the executable's SHA-256 against a SHA256SUMS from the same release, which proves integrity, not origin; attestation checks are a manual `gh attestation verify` (SECURITY.md:55-81; docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md:166-169). Printed join commands run `node -e '<check>'` and then `npx` on the downloaded package (lib/invocation.js:54). The Windows executable is not code-signed (docs/executables.md:75-84).

Platform limits: the Linux standalone executable needs glibc 2.28+ (not Alpine/musl or CentOS 7; install.sh:48-65); the source and npm routes need Node 22+ (bin/agent-console.mjs:14-21); WSL2 is not in the support table or CI, and joining from WSL needs --advertise plus port forwarding (README.md:257-266; server.js:396-399); the Projects view runs /usr/bin/git on non-Windows (lib/gitstats.js:29-40), so a git installed elsewhere would not be found by that path (not tested here).

Network and security posture when shared: --listen exposes the reporting port to private networks; the join page is plain HTTP and alterable on-path (SECURITY.md:172-197); the sign-in cookie is HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict but 127.0.0.1 cookies are sent to every local port (SECURITY.md:131-135; lib/hub/admin.js:212); no at-rest encryption, SSO/roles or persistent audit log (docs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md:203-210; docs/security/ENTERPRISE-FAQ.md:80-81); the hub's machine keeps project names, full paths and branches in names.json (docs/security/DATA-FLOWS.md:97-101, 114); some CodeQL alerts are dismissed rather than fixed (THREAT-MODEL.md:194-199) and open alerts are described as being triaged (ENTERPRISE-FAQ.md:154-156); a reporter can report false numbers for itself (THREAT-MODEL.md:127-128).

Licensing: the code is MIT (LICENSE:1-21; package.json:58), but the MIT grant does not cover the LockedIn Labs name or marks and a modified version must not be presented as a LockedIn Labs product (README.md:832-838); the brand assets (public/brand, app icons, docs/brand lockups, screenshots) are the company's own (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:54-66); IBM Plex fonts are OFL 1.1 and the standalone executables embed Node.js with its bundled components' licences (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:8-20, 34-45); the Anthropic and OpenAI marks belong to their owners (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:22-32).

checks.statement: Reads both tools' local transcripts read-only (Claude Code: $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects, ~/.claude/projects, ~/.config/claude/projects; Codex: $CODEX_HOME/sessions plus archived_sessions, or ~/.codex/sessions plus ~/.codex/archived_sessions). No other tool is parsed. README and INSTALL.md are written so Claude Code or Codex can install it. Claude Code only: policy apply writes repo-scoped .claude/agents, .claude/settings.json and a hook (PreToolUse, PreModelSwitch), with private backups and policy remove. There is no Codex enforcement adapter. Claude Code OTel metrics can go to /v1/metrics with --interop. No plugin, skill, slash command or context-supply mechanism.

checks.statement: Measures provider usage (input, output, cache-creation and cache-read tokens) from the local logs Claude Code and Codex write; verified: partial (Codex cache-write/uncached input depend on cache_write_input_tokens, shown only in synthetic fixtures).

Uncached input is null unless cacheWrite is present (357-359, 403-404). test/collector-parsers.test.js:18-19 is a synthetic counters fixture.
